_comment: The GPU types the pool knows. vendor: nvidia (default) or amd; an amd row also carries pci_ids and gfx_target and is judged by those (vault 30). names: every string nvidia-smi prints for the type. vram_mib: the nominal size; a card is accepted inside nominal x [0.90, 1.05] unless vram_mib_min / vram_mib_max give a measured window. counts: the box sizes admitted for the type (a rental takes the whole box); default [1, 2, 4, 8]. status: qualified = admitted; listed = known but not admitted. Only the RTX5090 has been run on a real card. The other six are admitted on Lium's names and sizes (gpu_spec_table.py, 10/5) and on the proof built for their architectures, not yet on a run of our own: confirm each on a real card before the compute share pays. RTXPRO6000 carries a floor of 95000 MiB (both editions report 97887): at the default 0.90 floor the proof's fill floor for it would sit inside an H100's window. RTX3090 and RTX4090 (10/8) are the entry cards an individual owns; listed until one of each is run. They share one 24 GB window (a 3090 reports 24576, a 4090 24564), so the fill cannot tell them apart: the kernel does, the proof's sm_89 code does not load on a 3090 (sm_86), and a 4090 answering a 3090's challenge is a dearer card claiming a cheaper one. AMD rows (10/8, vault 30 §4, §8; 31 step 4): matched on vendor + pci_ids (sysfs device id), never on a name; names is the display name; gfx_target is what the KFD topology reports and what the proof binary is built for; compute_cap on an AMD row is the same string. All listed until the first MI300X run (31 step 1) sets the proof's reference; MI350 is one row for the MI350X and the MI355X (same memory, same gfx950). The MI300X and MI325X boxes the market sells are 8x; a 1x is the measurement VM. PCI ids: MI300X 0x74a1, MI325X 0x74a5, MI300A 0x74a0, MI350X/MI355X 0x75a0/0x75a3, R9700 0x7590, from the amdgpu id table (verify each on a real card before it leaves listed). MI350P and MI455X wait for ids.
